name: Saxon Switzerland
reference_area: Saxon Switzerland climbing overview and rules
overview: One of the world's largest and most distinctive sandstone climbing landscapes, with more than 21,000 routes on approved free-standing towers. The legally embedded Saxon ethic is essential: climb only permitted dry peaks, use textile protection rather than metal gear, do not use chalk, stay on approved approaches, and check seasonal nesting closures.

name: Montserrat
overview: A vast Catalan conglomerate massif of rounded towers, long ridges, and steep walls, with more than 5,600 routes ranging from single-pitch sport climbing to serious multipitch adventures. Bolt spacing and route character vary widely, and the official zoning map includes permanent and seasonal nesting closures.

name: La Pedriza
overview: A huge granite labyrinth in the Sierra de Guadarrama north of Madrid, combining roughly 3,470 documented boulder problems with 2,675 roped routes. Runout slabs, cracks, multipitch domes, annual nesting restrictions, and quota-controlled Canto Cochino vehicle access all shape trip planning.

name: Zillertal
overview: One of Austria's largest and most varied climbing valleys, with roughly 1,300 boulder problems, 700 sport routes, and dozens of multipitch lines on granite and gneiss. Snowmelt, summer storms, private-land parking, and tolled or seasonal upper-valley roads should be checked before choosing a sector.

name: Chironico
overview: Ticino's largest bouldering destination, with more than two thousand gneiss problems spread through forested sectors above the Leventina valley. Cool, dry shoulder-season weather is ideal; respect private land, signed parking, and any sector-specific restrictions.
classic_routes: Fight Club (V15, boulder) | Big Paw (V14, boulder)

name: Cresciano
overview: A foundational world-class Ticino bouldering hub of technical slabs, compression lines, and steep testpieces on fine-grained gneiss. The 1,850-problem guide total spans 27 areas in the broader Riviera district, including Cresciano and nearby valleys. Driving the alpine road to the upper boulders is prohibited: park in the village, keep access clear, respect private property, and avoid wet rock.
classic_routes: Dreamtime (V15, boulder) | The Story of Two Worlds (V15, boulder)

name: Mallorca
overview: A coherent island destination with more than fifteen hundred sport routes plus one of the world's premier deep-water-soloing circuits. Access is highly sensitive and several former crags have been restricted or lost; use current local guidance. Season and wind determine whether inland crags or coastal sectors work best, while DWS demands calm seas, safe exits, and team rescue readiness.

name: El Chorro
overview: A long-established Andalusian winter destination with a huge limestone inventory ranging from roadside sport crags to adventurous multipitch lines above the gorge. Climbing above the Caminito del Rey is prohibited year-round, and other sectors have authorization or seasonal closures; heat, loose rock, railway boundaries, and parking make the current regulation map essential.

name: Chulilla
overview: A premier Spanish limestone destination built around exceptionally long, endurance-heavy sport routes on both sides of a deep canyon. An 80-meter rope is standard for many sectors; aspect, heat, parking, and occasional closures should drive daily planning.

name: San Vito lo Capo
overview: A major Mediterranean limestone destination on Sicily's northwest coast, with dense sport crags, sea-cliff settings, and longer multipitch objectives. Marine corrosion has left some hardware suspect or broken, so consult the current problem-bolt and rebolting list before climbing; also respect parking, private property, and route restrictions.

name: Gastlosen
overview: A striking chain of limestone towers in the Swiss Prealps with a dense mix of single-pitch sport climbing and long multipitch routes. Snowmelt, alpine storms, approach conditions, and route length make summer through early autumn the dependable window.
classic_routes: Hallo Marco (5.10a, sport) | Gasterix (5.11d, sport) | Yeah Man (5.14a, sport)

name: Varazze
overview: A world-class riverbed and forest bouldering destination on the Italian Riviera, with more than a thousand metabasite problems and a famous concentration of difficult lines. Winter friction is ideal; avoid wet rock and follow the latest parking and access agreements.
classic_routes: Gioia (V16, boulder)

name: Riglos (Mallos de Riglos)
overview: Iconic 300-meter conglomerate towers above a small Aragonese village, offering steep, exposed multipitch climbing on embedded cobbles. Many routes are bolted but remain committing; heat, wind, loose rock, and complex descents reward conservative planning. Check current Monumento Natural and climbing-federation notices for wildlife, fire, and temporary closures.
classic_routes: Fiesta de los Bíceps (5.11d, sport) | Mosquitos (5.10d, sport) | Espolón del Adamello (5.10b, sport)

name: Railay & Tonsai
overview: Southeast Asia's landmark limestone destination, reached by boat and built around steep tufa sport climbing, sea views, and a smaller set of multipitch routes. Coastal corrosion makes bolt material and rebolting status a critical route-level check, even on popular lines.
classic_routes: The Groove Tube (5.9-, sport) | Humanality (5.10c/d, sport) | Lord of the Thai's (5.12b, sport) | Crystal Flame (5.10c, sport)

name: Thakhek / Pha Tam Kam
overview: Laos's principal climbing destination, centered on steep tufa and pocketed limestone beside Green Climbers Home, with hundreds of sport routes and a few multipitches. The climbing season generally runs October through May; winter is best, while late dry-season heat and regional smoke can matter. The KOP–Thakhek border crossing is not available to every nationality, so verify current visa and border eligibility before booking flights.
classic_routes: Kim und Struppi (5.10a, sport) | White Rabbit (5.10-, sport) | From Dusk til Dawn (5.10d, sport) | Jungle King (5.12b, sport)

name: Serra do Cipó
overview: Brazil's best-known sport-climbing destination, with hundreds of limestone routes across dozens of sectors in the cerrado landscape of Minas Gerais. The dry season is most dependable; access and parking vary by sector and should be checked with the current local guide.

name: Frey / Cerro Catedral
overview: More than fifty golden granite spires surround Refugio Frey above Bariloche, creating one of South America's deepest alpine-rock destinations. Reaching the refugio requires a substantial hike and reservation; fast-changing Patagonian weather and self-reliant multipitch skills are central to the trip.
classic_routes: Diedro de Jim (5.8, trad) | Sifuentes-Weber (5.9, trad) | Imagínate (5.10b, trad)

name: Cochamó Valley
overview: A remote Chilean valley of thousand-meter granite walls, often compared with Yosemite and known for committing cracks, faces, and big-wall routes. Entry requires a long approach and advance camping planning; the community-managed valley expects reservations, low-impact travel, and strong self-rescue skills.
classic_routes: E.Z. Does It (5.10+, trad) | Bienvenidos a mi Insomnia (5.11a, trad) | Al Centro y Adentro (5.11c, trad) | Positive Affect (5.12a, trad)

name: Chaltén Massif
overview: The globally iconic Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre massif, with hundreds of serious alpine rock, ice, mixed, and aid routes on Patagonian granite spires. Weather windows are short and consequences high; current Los Glaciares registration, fees, conditions, and rescue limitations must be checked.
classic_routes: Supercanaleta (WI4 M5, alpine) | Via dei Ragni (WI5 M4+ A2, alpine) | Chiaro di Luna (5.10+, trad)

name: Hampi
overview: A globally distinctive granite bouldering landscape woven through Hampi's UNESCO-listed ruins and surrounding villages. Climbing access can be sensitive and locally variable: use local guidance, avoid monuments and protected structures, and treat the route count and grades as guidebook estimates rather than an official inventory.

name: Darran Mountains
overview: New Zealand's premier alpine-rock district, spanning roadside sport, traditional multipitch, long alpine rock routes, and winter mixed objectives around Milford Road and Homer Hut. Fiordland weather, avalanche risk, Milford Road status, hut booking, and remote rescue logistics are material on every visit.
classic_routes: North Buttress (NZ 17, trad) | Quiet Earth (NZ 21, trad) | Vindication (NZ 25, sport)

name: Valle de los Cóndores
reference_area: Valle de los Cóndores climbing area
overview: A high Andean basalt destination near Talca with hundreds of steep sport routes, striking columns, and a growing international reputation. The remote plateau has no public transport, a rough access road, harsh weather, and winter snow, so vehicle and condition planning are essential.

name: Los Arenales
overview: A remote high-Andes granite destination southwest of Mendoza, with 456 traditional and sport routes plus 34 boulder problems on walls and spires up to 750 meters. Single-pitch cragging and long multipitch objectives coexist; access-road conditions, altitude, storms, self-rescue, and the absence of nearby services demand careful preparation.

name: La Huasteca
overview: An urban-adjacent limestone canyon west of Monterrey with hundreds of bolted crag routes and adventure walls approaching a thousand feet. The dependable season is fall through early spring; summer heat can be extreme, and access or security conditions should be checked locally.

name: Suesca
overview: The birthplace of Colombian climbing, with a long sandstone escarpment and hundreds of traditional, sport, and multipitch routes an easy trip from Bogotá. Climbing is possible year-round, but the drier windows are best; respect railway, private-property, and reserve signage.

name: Piedra Parada / La Buitrera
overview: A Patagonian sport destination centered on the long volcanic-tuff walls of La Buitrera canyon and the freestanding Piedra Parada monolith. The official climbing season is October through April; climbing is prohibited May through September, and the remote setting requires water and transport planning.
